ai.title: Update npm-app-release-prod.yml workflow
ai.summary: Workflow step renamed to 'Commit and push version bumpAdd commentMore actions' to reflect direct push behavior. Release commit logic replaced with `git stash`, `git pull --rebase origin main`, and `git stash pop` to sync before committing `npm-app/release/package.json`. Removes Codebuff co-author trailers and broad `git add -A` in favor of targeted file staging.

eli5.text: The release-publishing automation now quietly syncs its local work with the shared main codebase before it saves the new version number and pushes it. Previously it would dump every pending change into one commit, so you sometimes saw messy commits or stray file changes mixed into the release. Now it only commits the version-number file, keeps its working files in sync, and no longer tags messages as being authored by Codebuff, so release logs read more predictably. It is in place on the production release branch (npm-app) and you would mainly notice it by checking the git log: the most recent release commit no longer carries the old co-author note and contains only the version bump, not a grab-bag of changes.

ai.title: Add env-overrides input to npm-app-release-build workflow
ai.summary: New `env-overrides` string input added to `.github/workflows/npm-app-release-build.yml`, accepting a JSON object to override default environment variables during the build process. The workflow logic now applies these overrides via `jq` after setting base secrets, replacing the hardcoded `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT` assignment. `npm-app-release-prod.yml` utilizes this new input to explicitly set `NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT` for production builds. This change decouples environment configuration from the build script, allowing flexible target environments without code changes.

eli5.text: When the system builds the production release, it can now accept a list of custom settings that override the default values, allowing different deployment targets without changing the build code. Previously, the production build always used the same hardcoded environment settings; now those settings come from a configurable input that the production workflow explicitly supplies. The staging workflow was also updated to support the same mechanism, though it does not yet pass any custom values. If you looked at the production release process today, you'd see it now carries an explicit set of environment overrides instead of relying on fixed defaults.
